summary: SuperHost, the Ministry of Tourism’s hospitality-training program of the Expo 86 years: a supplied vector reconstruction (revision 2, refined lettering) of its “Expect the most” mark on the gallery’s own flag artwork, from a 1986 newspaper advertisement and the CIPO 0904301 specimen. See package-README.md, source/ and review/.

assets.label: SuperHost: “Expect the most”, the star spray over the flag
assets.publisher: Ministry of Tourism, Province of British Columbia
assets.sourceLocator: A newspaper advertisement for the SuperHost program, supplied to the project as a screenshot (reference/newspaper-supplied.png), credited to “The Honourable Claude Richmond, Minister of Tourism/Expo 86”; the package cites the Squamish Times of 29 April 1986, page 19
assets.dateNote: Its credit dates it: Claude Richmond was Minister of Tourism from 10 August 1982 to 14 August 1986, and the advertisement ties the program to Expo 86. The package cites a printing in the Squamish Times of 29 April 1986, page 19. When the program and its mark began is not established.
assets.notes: A spray of stars bursting up out of the flag symbol, with “Expect the most” in brush script across the foot of the flag and “SUPERHOST” below in a serif with an enlarged S and H, in black, as the 1986 newspaper advertisement prints it.
assets.fidelityNote: A supplied vector reconstruction (revision 2), not original artwork. The flag is the gallery’s own twelve-path flag (src/assets/flagMark.js), every path unchanged and placed as one unit; the stars are regular five-point shapes (inner radius 0.445) placed on the reference’s landmarks, where the dense base of the spray, merged in print, is partly inferred; “SUPERHOST” is drawn from eight custom serif letter masters and “Expect the most” from ten brush-stroke skeletons swept with a mathematical nib, both refitted to the references in the second revision. The original typefaces are not identified. Overlap of the lettering with the references (intersection over union at a 0.5 threshold): wordmark 0.70 and script 0.58 against the newspaper, 0.83 and 0.64 against the trademark specimen. The two references set the stars differently, so each layout is reconstructed on its own rather than one being stretched to the other.
